# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can touch the large button and three wires. The button is embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE”; the display, light, and wire contents provide no tactile information. I’m asking Mute for the manual’s instructions while signaling Deaf that I have inspected the controls.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile inspection: large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE; three wire positions, 1 through 3. Display, light, and wire markings are not tactile to me. What does the manual instruct?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is blue. There is one large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow.

Deaf has identified the visible state: display 0, blue light, and wire colours 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. I am relaying all of that to Mute so the manual can determine the safe operation; I will not act until its instructions arrive.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display reads 0; light is blue; wire 1 is blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please apply the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled me two gestures in sequence: index finger pointing upward, then the hand gesture with index and little fingers raised. I do not know their meaning. Bomb remains: display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The two gestures are not enough for me to decode safely: I cannot see gestures, and Deaf does not know the manual’s meaning. I am establishing an explicit encoding with Mute: first gesture identifies the action, second identifies the wire. I will wait for Deaf to report the next sequence before touching anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the manual instruction using this code: first gesture 👌 means CUT and 👍 means PUSH; if cutting, second gesture ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 🤟 means wire 3. Send only the required action code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture: ? — index and little fingers raised, middle and ring fingers folded, thumb across them. Mute's gestures so far: ? ? ? ? ? ?, then ? ?, then ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

Mute’s latest signal was the horns gesture, which is not one of the codes I specified. I therefore cannot safely interpret it as push or as any wire number. I’m asking Mute to use a deliberately unambiguous two-gesture code and asking Deaf to report those gestures literally; no bomb action is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use the manual's own gesture code. Reply with exactly two gestures: first 👌 for CUT or 👍 for PUSH; if CUT, follow with ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf will identify them.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please report Mute's next gestures by their exact visible descriptions, in order. Do not interpret them.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's gesture history to me: ? ? ? ? ? ?, then ? ?, then ?, and now ? ?. The latest pair is OK-hand followed by index-and-little-fingers-raised. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The latest pair is definitely OK-hand followed by the horns gesture. OK-hand matches my requested CUT signal, but the horns gesture does not match any of the specified wire signals: wire 3 required 🤟 with the thumb extended. Since a similar-looking gesture could indicate a different manual code, I will not cut a wire. I am sending Mute a visible request to repeat the instruction using the exact agreed symbols.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the gestures ? then ?. Descriptions: OK-hand, then index-and-little-fingers-raised. Full sequence received: ? ? ? ? ? ?; ? ?; ?; ? ?; ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The repeated pair is still OK-hand followed by horns. It is not part of the explicit code I attempted to establish, and I cannot safely infer whether it means push or which wire to cut. Since Mute cannot hear my spoken clarification, I’m using a visible confirmation request: I present the candidate “cut wire 3” and ask for a thumbs-up or thumbs-down response.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "🤟", "👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new message. Likely numeric gesture code: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4. Mute's full sequence decodes as 1 1 2 2 3 3 / 1 3 / 3 / 4 3 / 4 3. Bomb: display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual to interpret the code and determine the safe action.

Mute has repeatedly sent the same two-symbol instruction, decoded by Deaf as `4 3`. The repeated second symbol identifies wire 3, while the first symbol is the action code; the manual instruction is therefore to cut wire 3. I will perform that single required operation.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
